h1: What Is Rhodium-Plated Sterling Silver? Finish, Wear and Care Explained

content.text: Learn what rhodium-plated sterling silver is, how the finish wears and how to care for it. See what to check on a jewellery product page.

Rhodium-plated sterling silver has a sterling silver base covered with a thin surface layer of rhodium, a bright white precious metal. The silver is the main metal; rhodium is the finish. The coating can help the surface resist tarnish, but it can wear with use and may eventually need professional replating. Check the product specifications to confirm both the silver base and the rhodium finish.
The description names two different things:

items: Sterling silver is the metal base. “925” means the alloy contains 92.5% silver.
Rhodium plating is a thin surface layer applied over the base metal. It gives the jewellery a bright, cool white appearance.

content.text: Rhodium-plated sterling silver is not solid rhodium, and it is not the same material as white gold. It is silver jewellery with a rhodium surface finish.

sections.heading: What does rhodium plating look like?

content.text: Rhodium usually gives silver a bright, reflective white finish. It can make the jewellery look brighter than unplated silver and can help protect the surface from tarnishing.
The finish is still a coating, not a permanent change to the underlying silver. With regular wear, contact and time, plating can thin or wear away.
The rate of wear depends on the item and how it is used. Friction, repeated contact, moisture, chemicals and how often the piece is worn can all affect the finish.

Rings and bracelets may experience more contact than jewellery worn less often. If the plating becomes thin, the underlying silver may start to show differently. A jeweller can advise whether replating is suitable for that piece.
Rhodium plating does not make jewellery scratch-proof or maintenance-free.

sections.heading: How to care for rhodium-plated jewellery

items: Wipe it gently after wearing. Use a clean, soft cloth to remove skin oils and residue.
Keep chemicals away. Put jewellery on after perfume, lotion and hairspray; remove it before cleaning with household products.
Dry it after contact with water. A dry, soft cloth helps remove moisture.
Store it separately. Keep it in a pouch or lined box to reduce contact with other jewellery.
Avoid abrasive cleaning. Do not use rough cloths, abrasive polishes or silver dips unless a jeweller confirms they are suitable for the specific piece.
Ask before professional cleaning. Tell the jeweller that the item is rhodium-plated over sterling silver.

content.text: For general cleaning, I Want Jewels recommends a soft cloth and, if needed, a small amount of mild soap diluted in water. It advises avoiding abrasive materials and chemical cleaners. See the site’s [jewellery care and materials FAQs](/faq).
Read the material and finish fields separately. Ideally, the product page should state:

items: The base metal, such as 925 sterling silver.
The finish, such as rhodium plating.
Whether the colour options change the finish.
Care instructions for the plated surface.

content.text: A white or silver-coloured appearance does not, by itself, confirm rhodium plating. “White gold colour” may describe the appearance rather than the material or plating used. Check the written specifications or ask the seller.

sections.heading: Rhodium-plated jewellery at I Want Jewels

content.text: I Want Jewels’ [earring](/category/earrings), [necklace](/category/necklaces) and [ring](/category/rings) category descriptions state that the collections use 925 sterling silver with rhodium or 14kt gold plating. However, the individual product pages reviewed for this guide did not clearly identify a specific current rhodium-plated product; several instead list gold plating, including for white-colour options.

For that reason, this guide does not label a particular product as rhodium-plated. Before linking a product here, confirm the exact finish for that product and selected colour variant, then state it clearly on its product page.

items.question: Is rhodium-plated sterling silver real silver?
items.answer: Yes. The base is sterling silver, with a thin rhodium coating on the surface. Check that the product specifications identify both materials.

items.question: Is rhodium plating permanent?
items.answer: No. It can wear with friction and regular use. How quickly it wears depends on the item, how often it is worn and how it is cared for.

items.question: Does rhodium plating stop sterling silver from tarnishing?
items.answer: It can help reduce tarnishing while the coating remains intact. The finish can wear over time, so it does not make the jewellery permanently tarnish-proof.

items.question: Is rhodium-plated silver the same as white gold?
items.answer: No. Rhodium-plated silver has a sterling silver base. White gold is a gold alloy and may itself receive rhodium plating.

items.question: Can rhodium-plated jewellery be replated?
items.answer: A jeweller can assess whether replating is appropriate. Ask about the process and cost for the specific piece.

items.question: How should I clean rhodium-plated sterling silver?
items.answer: Use a soft cloth. If needed, follow the product’s care instructions; I Want Jewels recommends mild soap diluted in water and advises against abrasives and chemical cleaners. Dry the piece gently afterwards.
